question: In chemical reaction N₂ + xH₂ → 2NH₃, what is the value of x?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical equation **N2 + xH2 → 2NH3** represents the reaction between **nitrogen and hydrogen** to form **ammonia.**
 
• The balanced equation states that **two molecules of ammonia **are formed for every **one molecule **of nitrogen and **three molecules** of hydrogen.
 
• Therefore, the value of x represents the number of **hydrogen molecules **required to react with **one molecule **of nitrogen.
 
• By comparing the number of hydrogen atoms on each side of the equation, it can be determined that **x = 3**.
 
• This is because there are** six hydrogen atoms** on the product side (2NH₃) and only **two hydrogen atoms** on the reactant side (xH₂).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nitrogen fixation** is the process of converting **atmospheric nitrogen **into a** usable form **by living organisms.
 
• This reaction is an example of nitrogen fixation, as ammonia can be used by** plants **as a **source of nitroge**n for** growth.**
 
• The **Haber-Bosch process **is an** industrial method** used to produce** ammonia **on a large scale.
 
• It involves the reaction of **nitrogen and hydrogen** under **high pressure and temperature**, using a **catalyst.**
